description.value: The study examined resting-state functional connectivity of the bilateral habenula in autistic and neurotypical individuals, including diagnostic group differences, age-related developmental variability, functional decoding, and associations with autism-related phenotypic measures.

design.value: A large-scale, multisite, cross-sectional observational study using resting-state functional MRI data from the ABIDE I and II datasets. Participant-level habenula connectivity maps were entered into group-level regression models comparing ASD and NT participants and testing age-related and phenotypic associations while controlling for sex and scanning site.

description.value: The BRIEF GEC T-score measured executive function by compiling scores from three composite indexes testing behavior regulation, emotional recognition, and cognitive regulation; executive function encompassed working memory, flexible thinking, and self-control.

The DLS domain measured adaptive behavior encompassing everyday tasks necessary for independent living, including personal care, household responsibilities, and community activities such as maintaining hygiene, preparing meals, and managing money and time.

source_definition.value: Diagnosis (ASD, NT) was included as a categorical factor.
Age at scan was included as a continuous factor.
Sex was controlled for in the group-level regression models.
Scanning site was controlled for in the regression models; the data were acquired across 24 scanning sites.
Age-by-group interactions were tested to probe for age-related changes in habenula connectivity between the ASD and NT groups.
SM refers to the extent to which an individual is generally motivated to engage in social-interpersonal behavior and was measured with the 11-item SRS Social Motivation subscale.
SC refers to reciprocal and expressive communication in social situations and was measured with the 22-item SRS Social Communication subscale.
EF refers to working memory, flexible thinking, and self-control and was measured through the BRIEF Global Executive Composite Score T-score.
DLS are a measure of adaptive behavior encompassing everyday tasks necessary for independent living and were measured with the DLS domain of Vineland-2nd edition.

task_description.value: Resting-state functional MRI data were used to calculate whole-brain functional connectivity maps from averaged left and right habenula time series.

description.value: Resting-state functional MRI data were acquired across the 24 scanning sites using 3T MRI scanners.
For all participants, a T1-weighted structural image was collected and used for registration to Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space.
Data were preprocessed using fMRIPrep 23.1.3 with manual and automated quality control, followed by motion-based participant/session/run exclusion and denoising using AFNI’s 3dTproject.

steps.value: Anatomical images were intensity-corrected, skull-stripped, segmented, and spatially normalized to MNI152 space.
Preprocessed data underwent both manual and automated quality control.
Participants receiving a “fail” rating from any independent rater for ABIDE I were manually excluded.
MRIQC 23.1.0 was used to inspect, flag, and remove participants, sessions, or runs with framewise displacement greater than 0.35mm or fewer than 100 usable time points following motion censoring.
Denoising was performed on the remaining participants using AFNI’s 3dTproject, which uses a linear regression model for nuisance time series from each voxel.

model_settings.value: For each participant, averaged left and right habenula ROI time series were entered into a general linear model to generate whole-brain correlation maps; resulting maps were Fisher r-to-z transformed.
Diagnosis was modeled as a categorical factor and age as a continuous factor, controlling for sex and scanning site, using AFNI’s 3dLMEr.

Z-transformed participant-level correlation maps from participants aged 5–21 years were analyzed for age-by-group interactions, controlling for sex and scanning site. Beta coefficients were extracted from 5mm spherical masks centered on significant cluster peaks and entered into linear regression models for each group.

estimator.value: linear effects model and linear regression

model_settings.value: Z-scored beta coefficients were extracted from clusters showing atypical habenula connectivity using a 3mm spherical mask. Clusters were tested for phenotypic main effects among ASD participants and phenotypic interactions between ASD and NT groups, with group as a categorical factor and age as a continuous factor, controlling for sex and scanning site. Correlation coefficients were entered into linear regression models as a function of each phenotypic subscore.
